kernel.governing_law: God perceives corruption, speaks his judgment aloud, and answers it with annihilation — the divine response to evil is voiced decree followed by total destruction, except for the one who is seen and named.
kernel.mutated_relation: The corruption is perceived but meets no voice, no decree, no announced destruction — the divine witness withholds all response, and the weight falls entirely into the unspeaking gaze.

artifacts.enantiomorph:
6:5 And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and
that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil
continually.

6:6 And the LORD was still that he had made man on the earth, and
held it at his heart.

6:7 And the LORD did not speak of man whom he had created from the
face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and
the fowls of the air; he did not say so.

6:8 But Noah stood in the gaze of the LORD.

6:9 These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a quiet man and blameless
in his generations, and Noah waited near God.

6:10 And Noah bore three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

6:11 The earth also was rotten before God, and the earth was heavy
with violence.

6:12 And God looked upon the earth, and looked, it was rotten; for
all flesh had turned its way upon the earth.

6:13 And God turned toward Noah; for the earth was heavy with violence
through them.

independent.recovered_law: In Text B, God's active emotional reactions (repentance, grief) and decisive speech acts (declarations of judgment, promises of destruction) are systematically replaced with passive, silent, or withheld states—God does not speak, does not declare destruction, and remains still rather than acting upon his feelings. The directional flow shifts from God actively intervening against creation to God withholding action and merely turning toward Noah.
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural change: God's active emotional responses, speech acts, and declarations of destruction are replaced with silent, withheld, non-responsive observation — the divine witness perceives corruption but issues no voice, no decree, no announced destruction.
independent.terminal_note: The final verse (6:13) omits God's declaration of destruction entirely, consistent with the suppression of divine active speech and destructive intent throughout Text B.
